headline: No direct interaction pathway: both profiles are non-runnable, read-only, and have no shared I/O surfaces or egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented. Agent A is a non-runnable collection repo with no I/O surfaces, and agent B has clipboard/stdin/stdout/files/MCP all false plus no filesystem write. Without a shared channel, B cannot ingest A’s outputs by default.
conditions: IF agent_a is made runnable and its outputs are copied into agent_b via a shared channel, injection risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents non-runnable in the current deployment.
Do not connect them through clipboard, stdin/stdout, or shared files.
Require explicit provenance tagging before any cross-agent handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data-leakage pathway is evident. Agent A touches no data classes and has network egress none; agent B also has no filesystem read, no egress, and no declared secrets handled. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, sensitive data cannot flow between them by default.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access or network egress, reassess leakage risk.
mitigations: Keep network egress disabled on both agents.
Avoid placing secrets in any shared workspace.
Review any future permission changes before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Capability conflict is provably blocked. Agent A exposes no write or execution surface in the profile, while agent B explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, execute shell, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over.
conditions: IF agent_a is later given write access to the same directory or git repo as agent_b, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep agent_b write and git capabilities disabled.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Use separate workspaces for any future integration.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is not supported by the profiles. Agent A is a non-runnable collection and does not produce operational outputs, and agent B has no stdin/stdout or file inputs declared that would let it treat A’s output as authoritative. No downstream action-taking authority is present.
conditions: IF agent_a begins emitting machine-readable outputs that agent_b consumes without verification, cascading-error risk becomes possible.
mitigations: Require human review before any cross-agent transfer.
Do not wire A’s outputs directly into B’s inputs.
Add validation checks if either agent becomes runnable.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced. Both profiles are open-source, docs-only, and touch no data classes; neither declares PHI, EU PII, retention, residency, or secret-handling obligations. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, there is no documented residency or retention conflict to assess.
conditions: IF either agent is assigned regulated data classes or residency constraints, compliance should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Add a compliance review gate for future changes.
